findings.message:
Internal error text is returned to clients in the invalid_grant description: The Token handler passes the raw store error into the OAuth error description (`oauthError(w, "invalid_grant", err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)`). ExchangeCode in session.go produces distinct internal messages such as `fmt.Errorf("redirect_uri mismatch")` and `fmt.Errorf("code not found or expired")`, and verifyPKCE emits `fmt.Errorf("PKCE verification failed")` / `fmt.Errorf("invalid_grant")`. These are leaked verbatim to unauthenticated callers of POST /token.
Scenario: An attacker probing POST /token with guessed codes and redirect_uri values can distinguish 'code not found or expired' from 'redirect_uri mismatch' from 'PKCE verification failed', which reveals whether a code exists, whether it is still live, and which validation step failed, aiding targeted guessing or reconnaissance.
Keep the detailed reason server-side and return a stable public description: `slog.Warn("token exchange rejected", "err", err)` then `oauthError(w, "invalid_grant", "invalid_grant", http.StatusBadRequest)`. Alternatively define typed errors in session.go and map them to fixed, non-informative descriptions.
